title: Mass moment of inertia: why a flywheel resists changes in its spin

explain.say: A potter's wheel keeps turning after a kick, and a car engine has a heavy flywheel that smooths out the jerky push of each cylinder. Both rely on rotational inertia: spinning things resist changes to their spin. Mass alone is not the whole story. Look at the flywheel on its shaft.

draw.text: Flywheel: solid steel disc, 50 kg, radius 0.3 m

explain.say: For rotation, what counts is the mass moment of inertia, I: each bit of mass times its distance from the axle squared, all added up. Mass far from the axle counts much more. For a solid disc, I is a half m r squared: a half times 50 times 0.3 squared, which is 2.25 kilogram metres squared. See the big wheel?

explain.say: Now compare. Put the same 50 kilograms in a thin ring at 0.3 metres, and I doubles to 4.5, because every bit is at the rim. Shrink the disc to 0.15 metres and I drops to a quarter. Look at the bars. Why do racing bikes use light rims?

So the wheels speed up easily! Newton's second law for rotation is torque equals I times alpha, the angular acceleration. Our motor gives 9 newton metres to the 2.25 disc, so alpha equals 9 over 2.25, which is 4 radians per second squared. See the motor driving the shaft? How long to reach 31.4 radians per second?

explain.say: About 7.9 seconds. At that speed, 300 revolutions per minute, the flywheel stores a half I omega squared: a half times 2.25 times 31.4 squared, about 1.1 kilojoules. Well done! Real link: flywheels store energy in some city buses and racing cars. Challenge: how much energy at twice the speed?

faq.q: What is mass moment of inertia?
faq.a: It measures how hard it is to change a body's rotation about an axis: the sum of each small mass times its distance from the axis squared. Its unit is kilogram metre squared.

faq.q: Why does a ring have more inertia than a disc?
faq.a: All of a ring's mass sits at the full radius, while a disc has mass spread from the centre outwards. Since distance is squared, the ring's I is m r squared, twice the disc's half m r squared.
asks: ring vs disc moment of inertia

faq.q: How much energy does a flywheel store?
faq.a: Rotational kinetic energy is a half times I times omega squared, with omega in radians per second. Doubling the speed stores four times the energy.

faq.q: What is the rotational version of F = ma?
faq.a: Torque equals moment of inertia times angular acceleration. Torque plays the role of force and I plays the role of mass.

faq.q: What does a flywheel do in an engine?
faq.a: It stores energy during the power strokes and gives it back between them, so the crankshaft turns at a smoother speed.

facts: A solid disc has a mass moment of inertia of one half m r squared about its axis; a thin ring has m r squared.
Rotational kinetic energy equals one half I omega squared.
